newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. says hopes Japan will join 'open skies' pacts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says hopes Japan will join 'open skies' pacts.

text.p: The United States hopes that Japan will be prepared to negotiate an "open skies" pact as some other Asian nations are doing, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Economic and Business Affairs Alan Larson told reporters on Thursday.

He also said the United States would be willing to consider a phased approach to a pact with Japan, adding that Washington would entertain the possibility of revisions to a 1952 U.S.-Japan agreement on aviation.
Larson said the United States was negotiating "open skies" pacts with several Pacific Rim countries.
U.S. officials did not name the countries, but Japanese media reports have said they include Malaysia, New Zealand and Singapore.
"It is in Japan's interests to be part of this movement," he said. "The world is moving in this direction. Countries that delay or resist risk being left behind."
Japanese and U.S. officials will meet on Friday for "exploratory" talks on whether to resume official negotiations on aviation.
The talks have been deadlocked since August. The United States has been calling for "open skies" -- the lifting of government restrictions on international economic decisions made by airlines.
But Japan argues that open skies accords will lead to domination of international markets by U.S. carriers.
Larson denied that the current bilateral agreement was unbalanced in favour of U.S. carriers.
He said U.S. airlines had increased market share by being more competitive after the United States deregulated its aviation markets.
